title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
summary: Eleven countries took part in the competition in Bangkok. Teenage winner Carmelle Collado's winning dance song is a tribute to Filipino women.

image.caption: Carmelle Collado is the first Eurovision Asia championImage: Sakchai Lalit/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The Phillippines on Saturday became the first winner of the Asian version of the Eurovision Song Contest.
Who took part in the event and which songs were featured?

Eleven countries, including South Korea, Malaysia and Vietnam, took part in the song contest in the Thai capital, Bangkok. However, major nations in the region such as China, Japan and India were absent from the event.
19-year-old Carmelle Collado's dance song "Sobra-Sobra" (Too Much) won the competition. The song, which features lyrics in both English and Tagalog, is an empowering tribute to Filipino women.
The Philippines received 211 points in the competition, with Thailand in second place with 170 points. Vietnam placed third with 164 points, while Malaysia landed in fourth place on 152 points.

blocks.caption: Thai duo Mang X Daou came in second place with their romantic pop tune 'Aroma' Image: Chanakarn Laosarakham/AFP

blocks.text: National juries in the participating countries and the viewing audience awarded the points.

blocks.caption: Vietnam's Toc Tien performed the lively song 'Em Tien' on leaves of the lotus, a flower associated with her country Image: Sakchai Lalit/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The competition featured motifs inspired by host city Bangkok, with the participants making their way to the stage on tuk-tuks and waving the flag of the countries they represent in a parade.

blocks.caption: Malaysia's Aina Abdul performed the ballad 'Bluest Sky' with water being used to represent the song's emotional buildup Image: Chanakarn Laosarakham/AFP

blocks.text: Will the Eurovision Song Contest Asia become a sensation?
The contest featured some references to the camp European competition. Bulgarian singer Dara performed "Bangaranga," the song which won the Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna in May.

It's unclear whether Eurovision Song Contest Asia will be as popular as the original competition, which received 131 million viewers this year. Tickets for the Bangkok event were still available just hours before it kicked off.
In 2022, a US spinoff, the American Song Contest, featured acts from all 50 US states. The competition, hosted by rapper Snoop Dogg and American Idol star Kelly Clarkson, only lasted for one season.
